mainTopic: Blessings over places of miracles, ברכת הגומל, and lists of רב יהודה
overview: This amud finishes the גמרא's explanation of a ברייתא that lists places where one makes a ברכה because of a miracle. First it completes the story of נחלי ארנון, where the mountains crushed enemies hiding in caves. It explains אבני אלגביש as hailstones that stopped because of משה and fell because of יהושע. It tells the oral tradition of עוג's mountain and briefly gives sources for the stone משה sat on, אשתו של לוט, and the wall of יריחו. The גמרא then asks how one can bless over אשתו של לוט, which was a punishment. It concludes that the place gets two blessings: ״דיין האמת״ for her and ״זוכר את הצדיקים״ for לוט. Next, רב lists four people who must thank ה׳, each learned from תהלים קז, and the גמרא teaches the blessing ״גומל חסדים טובים״, said before ten. A story about רב יהודה shows that answering אמן to others' blessing counts. The amud ends with more lists from רב יהודה: people who need protection, and things that lengthen life. The challenge to the long תפלה continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The ambush in the caves and the mountains closing in
steps.stepSummary: The אמוריים hid in caves to ambush ישראל, but the ארון flattened the mountains, the mountains pressed together, and the hidden enemies were crushed.
steps.simpleTranslation: They made caves for themselves and hid in them. They said: When ישראל passes here, we will kill them. They did not know that the ארון went ahead of ישראל and flattened the mountains in front of them. When the ארון came, the mountains pressed together and killed them, and their blood flowed down into נחלי ארנון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing its story about the miracle at נחלי ארנון. The enemies set up a hidden ambush, but a miracle wiped them out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The enemy's plan depended on the mountains staying where they were, so they could attack from the caves. Because the ארון traveled in front of ישראל and made the path flat, the mountains moved together and crushed them instead. This explains why נחלי ארנון is on the ברייתא's list of miracle places.

keyTerms.meaning: Caves or hollows in the rock
The streams, or valleys, of ארנון

steps.confusionAlert: This amud starts in the middle of the story. The people hiding in the caves are the אמוריים, the enemies of ישראל. They are not ישראל.

phrases.english: They made caves for themselves
and hid in them.

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרִי: כִּי חָלְפִי יִשְׂרָאֵל הָכָא — נִקְטְלִינּוּן,
phrases.english: They said: When Israel passes here, we will kill them,
but they did not know
that the Ark went ahead of Israel
and flattened the mountains before them.
Once the Ark came,
the mountains pressed against each other,
and killed them,
and their blood flowed down to the streams of Arnon.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story of the miracle at נחלי ארנון, which began on the previous amud.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The enemies hiding in the caves near ארנון were crushed when the mountains pressed together in front of the ארון.

steps.title: Discovering the miracle and the source in the פסוק
steps.stepSummary: את and והב see blood coming out from between the mountains, tell ישראל, and ישראל sings a שירה. The גמרא connects this to a פסוק in במדבר.
steps.simpleTranslation: When את and והב came, they saw blood coming out from between the mountains. They came and told ישראל, and ישראל sang a song. This is what is written: 'And the cascade of the streams that turned toward the dwelling of ער and leaned on the border of מואב.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how ישראל found out about the hidden miracle. It then shows a פסוק that hints to this story.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ישראל did not see the miracle happen, because the enemy was hidden. It became known only when את and והב noticed the blood. The פסוק about the 'cascade of the streams' leaning toward מואב is read as describing the mountains that moved together, which ties the story to the Torah.

keyTerms.meaning: Two people (described as lepers) who traveled at the back of the camp
A song of praise to ה׳
This is what is written; it introduces the פסוק behind a teaching
The cascade, or slope, of the streams

steps.whatToRemember: The miracle at נחלי ארנון was hidden at first and became known only through the blood. That is why ישראל sang, and why seeing this place calls for a ברכה.

phrases.english: When Et and Hev came,

phrases.aramaic: חֲזוֹ דְּמָא דְּקָא נָפֵיק מִבֵּינֵי טוּרֵי.
phrases.english: they saw blood coming out from between the mountains.
They came and told Israel,
and they sang a song.
This is what is written:
"And the cascade of the streams that turned toward the dwelling of Ar
and leaned on the border of Moab."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ארנון story and anchors it in a פסוק.
steps.raayaObject: The miracle of the mountains crushing the enemies at ארנון
steps.raayaSupportSource: במדבר כא:טו, 'ואשד הנחלים אשר נטה לשבת ער ונשען לגבול מואב'

steps.title: What are the hailstones of אלגביש?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next place on the ברייתא's list, אבני אלגביש, and asks what it means.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'The stones of אלגביש.' What are the stones of אלגביש?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next item on the list of miracle places and asks what the strange name means. This step sets up the explanation that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word אלגביש is unusual, so the גמרא needs to define it before we can know which miracle the ברייתא means. The answer will split the word into parts.

keyTerms.meaning: What is?; asks for a definition

phrases.english: The stones of Elgavish.
What are the stones of Elgavish?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from נחלי ארנון to the next miracle site on the ברייתא's list.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of the term אבני אלגביש and which miracle it refers to.

steps.title: Stones that stopped because of a man and fell because of a man
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא reads אלגביש as 'על גב איש': stones that hung in the air because of a man and later fell because of a man.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: These are stones that stood still because of a man, and came down because of a man.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question with a wordplay. It splits אלגביש into 'על גב' (because of) and 'איש' (a man).
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same hailstones are tied to two moments in history. First they stopped in mid-air, and later they fell. The next steps will identify each 'man'.
steps.confusionAlert: 'עמדו' here does not mean the stones stood on the ground. It means they stopped in mid-air and did not fall.

phrases.aramaic: תָּנָא: אֲבָנִים שֶׁעָמְדוּ עַל גַּב אִישׁ,
phrases.english: It was taught: Stones that stood still because of a man,
and came down because of a man.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 3.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: אלגביש means 'על גב איש': hailstones that stopped and later fell, each time because of a man.

steps.title: The first man is משה: the hail stopped
steps.stepSummary: The man whose merit made the stones stop is משה. The פסוק calls him 'איש', and in מכת ברד the hail stopped and did not reach the ground.
steps.simpleTranslation: They stood still because of a man: this is משה, as it is written, 'And the man משה was very humble.' And it is written, 'The thunder and the hail stopped, and rain did not pour down to the earth.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves who the first 'man' was by bringing two פסוקים. One shows משה is called 'איש', and the other shows the hail stopped because of him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof has two parts. First, the word 'איש' is linked to משה. Second, the פסוק about the end of מכת ברד shows the hail stopped without falling, which means it stayed suspended.

keyTerms.meaning: Did not pour down to the earth

phrases.aramaic: עָמְדוּ עַל גַּב אִישׁ — זֶה מֹשֶׁה,
phrases.english: They stood still because of a man: this is Moses,
as it is written: "And the man Moses was very humble,"
and it is written: "The thunder and the hail stopped,
and rain did not pour down to the earth."

steps.triggerLanguage: עָמְדוּ עַל גַּב אִישׁ — זֶה מֹשֶׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Identifies the first 'איש' from step 4.
steps.raayaObject: The hailstones stopped in mid-air because of משה

steps.title: The second man is יהושע: the stones fell
steps.stepSummary: The man in whose time the stones fell is יהושע. He is called 'איש', and in his war at בית חורון ה׳ threw great stones down on the enemy.
steps.simpleTranslation: They came down because of a man: this is יהושע, as it is written, 'Take for yourself יהושע בן נון, a man who has spirit in him.' And it is written, 'As they fled from before ישראל, while they were on the slope of בית חורון, ה׳ threw great stones down on them.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves who the second 'man' was in the same way. One פסוק shows יהושע is called 'איש', and another shows the stones fell in his war.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This finishes the explanation: the hail held back in משה's time was the same hail that later fell on the enemies of יהושע. So the site of אבני אלגביש is where those stones came down, and that is why one makes a ברכה there.

keyTerms.meaning: A man who has spirit in him
The slope, or descent, of בית חורון

steps.whatToRemember: אבני אלגביש = 'על גב איש': the same hailstones stopped because of משה and later fell on the enemy because of יהושע.

phrases.aramaic: יָרְדוּ עַל גַּב אִישׁ — זֶה יְהוֹשֻׁעַ,
phrases.english: They came down because of a man: this is Joshua,

phrases.aramaic: דִּכְתִיב: ״קַח לְךָ אֶת יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בִּן נוּן
phrases.english: as it is written: "Take for yourself Joshua the son of Nun,
a man who has spirit in him,"
and it is written: "And it was, as they fled from before the children of Israel,
while they were on the slope of Beit Choron,
that the Lord threw great stones down on them."

steps.triggerLanguage: יָרְדוּ עַל גַּב אִישׁ — זֶה יְהוֹשֻׁעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Identifies the second 'איש' and completes the definition.
steps.raayaObject: The hailstones fell because of יהושע

steps.title: The rock of עוג is known through oral tradition
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא turns to the next item on the list, the rock that עוג מלך הבשן tried to throw at ישראל, and says this is known from an oral tradition.
steps.simpleTranslation: The rock that עוג מלך הבשן tried to throw on ישראל: we know it through a tradition.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next miracle site and first tells us where the story comes from. This step sets up the story that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike the earlier miracles, this one is not written in any פסוק. The phrase 'גמרא גמירי לה' tells us it was passed down orally, so the גמרא will tell the story without quoting a verse.

keyTerms.meaning: עוג, king of בשן, a giant
It is known through an oral tradition

phrases.english: The rock that Og, King of Bashan, sought
to throw on Israel,
we know it through a tradition.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next miracle site in the ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The miracle of עוג's rock comes from an oral tradition, not from a פסוק.

steps.title: עוג's plan to crush the camp
steps.stepSummary: עוג figures the camp of ישראל is three פרסאות wide, so he plans to uproot a mountain of that size and throw it on them.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said: How big is the camp of ישראל? Three פרסאות. I will go, uproot a mountain three פרסאות big, throw it on them, and kill them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells us what עוג planned. He wanted a mountain big enough to cover the whole camp at once.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עוג's plan depended on size: he measured the camp and picked a mountain to match, so no one would escape. This sets up how ה׳ will ruin the plan.

keyTerms.meaning: פרסאות, a large unit of distance

phrases.english: He said: How big is the camp of Israel?
Three parasangs.

phrases.aramaic: אֵיזֵיל וְאֶיעֱקַר טוּרָא בַּר תְּלָתָא פַּרְסֵי
phrases.english: I will go and uproot a mountain three parasangs big,
and throw it on them, and kill them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins telling the tradition introduced in step 7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: עוג planned to kill all of ישראל with one mountain the size of their camp.

steps.title: ה׳ sends insects and the mountain drops onto עוג's neck
steps.stepSummary: עוג carries the mountain on his head, but ה׳ sends insects that bore a hole through it, and the mountain slips down around his neck.
steps.simpleTranslation: He went, uprooted a mountain three פרסאות big, and carried it on his head. הקדוש ברוך הוא sent insects onto it, they made a hole in it, and it slid down onto his neck.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells how ה׳ stopped עוג's plan. The mountain ended up stuck around עוג's own neck instead of falling on ישראל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Tiny insects defeated the plan of a giant. Because they bored a hole through the mountain, it fell around עוג and trapped him. The story continues next with what happened next to עוג.

keyTerms.meaning: They made a hole in it

phrases.aramaic: אֲזַל עֲקַר טוּרָא בַּר תְּלָתָא פַּרְסֵי
phrases.english: He went and uprooted a mountain three parasangs big
and carried it on his head.

phrases.aramaic: וְאַיְיתִי קוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא עֲלֵיהּ קַמְצֵי
phrases.english: And the Holy One, Blessed be He, brought insects upon it,
and they made a hole in it,
and it slid down onto his neck.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲזַל עֲקַר טוּרָא בַּר תְּלָתָא פַּרְסֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows how עוג's plan from step 8 failed through a miracle.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ה׳ ruined עוג's plan: insects bored through the mountain, and it fell around עוג's neck.

steps.title: עוג cannot get the mountain off his neck
steps.stepSummary: עוג tries to pull the mountain off his neck, but his teeth grow out to both sides and lock it in place.
steps.simpleTranslation: He wanted to pull the mountain off, but his teeth stretched out to this side and to that side, and he could not pull it off.
steps.whatsHappening: The story keeps going. עוג is stuck with the mountain around his neck, and when he tries to lift it off, his teeth grow long and trap it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the last step, the mountain slipped down around עוג's neck. Now we learn why he could not just lift it off: a miracle made his teeth grow outward and hold it in place. This new detail sets up the פסוק about 'teeth of the wicked' that comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: to pull it off / to remove it

phrases.english: He wanted to pull it off,
phrases.notes: 'It' means the mountain that slipped down around his neck.

phrases.english: his teeth stretched out to this side
and to that side
and he was not able to pull it off.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the עוג story from the mountain falling around his neck.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: עוג's teeth grew outward and trapped the mountain, so he could not remove it.

steps.title: A verse about the teeth of the wicked
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא connects the story to the פסוק 'You broke the teeth of the wicked.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And this is what is written: 'You broke the teeth of the wicked.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the story of עוג's teeth is hinted at in a פסוק in תהלים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק talks about 'teeth of the wicked,' and that fits the strange detail about עוג's teeth. There is a problem, though: the פסוק says the teeth were 'broken,' and in the story they grew longer. The next step fixes this.

keyTerms.meaning: and this is what is written

phrases.english: And this is what is written:
'You broke the teeth of the wicked.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a פסוק as a hint for the teeth detail in step 10.
steps.raayaObject: That עוג's teeth were affected when he fought against ישראל

steps.title: Reading the verse as 'You lengthened' the teeth
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן לקיש reads 'שברת' (You broke) as 'שרבבת' (You lengthened), so the פסוק matches the story.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this follows רבי שמעון בן לקיש, who said: What does it mean when it is written, 'You broke the teeth of the wicked'? Do not read it as 'You broke'; read it as 'You lengthened.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how the פסוק fits the story. It uses רבי שמעון בן לקיש's reading, which turns 'broke' into 'lengthened.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: Taken plainly, the פסוק says 'broke,' but in the story the teeth grew long. Through an 'אל תקרי' reading, רבי שמעון בן לקיש reads the word as 'שרבבת,' meaning stretched out. Now the פסוק lines up exactly with what happened to עוג.

keyTerms.meaning: do not read it as (a way of finding an extra layer of meaning in a word)
and this follows the view of רבי

steps.confusionAlert: 'אל תקרי' does not mean the text of the פסוק is being changed. The written word stays 'שברת.' The דרשה adds a second layer of meaning on top of it.

phrases.english: And this follows Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish.
For Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said:
What does it mean when it is written, 'You broke the teeth of the wicked'?
Do not read it as 'You broke'
but rather as 'You lengthened.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the פסוק in step 11 fits the long-teeth detail in step 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'שברת' is read as 'שרבבת': ה׳ made the teeth of the wicked grow long.

steps.title: משה strikes עוג's ankle and kills him
steps.stepSummary: משה, who is ten אמות tall, takes a ten-אמה axe, jumps ten אמות, hits עוג in the ankle, and kills him.
steps.simpleTranslation: How tall was משה? Ten אמות. He took an axe ten אמות long, jumped up ten אמות, struck עוג on his ankle, and killed him.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the end of the עוג story. משה kills the giant by hitting him in the ankle.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא adds up three tens: משה's height, the length of the axe, and the height of his jump. Together they come to thirty אמות, and even that only reached עוג's ankle. This shows how huge עוג was.

keyTerms.meaning: cubits (an אמה is about an arm's length)

steps.whatToRemember: The full story of the rock of עוג: he plans to throw a mountain on ישראל, insects bore a hole in it, it falls around his neck, his teeth lock it in place, and משה kills him. This miracle is why the place gets a ברכה.
steps.confusionAlert: 'משה כמה הוה' sounds like a question, but no one is challenging anything. It is just how the story tells us his height.

phrases.english: How tall was Moshe?
Ten cubits.
He took an axe ten cubits long,
jumped ten cubits,
struck him on his ankle, and killed him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the עוג story that began in step 7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: משה killed עוג with a blow to the ankle, reaching a total of thirty אמות.

steps.title: Source for the stone משה sat on
steps.stepSummary: The next item on the list is the stone משה sat on during the war with עמלק, and the גמרא gives the פסוק for it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the stone that משה sat on, as it is written: 'And משה's hands were heavy, and they took a stone and put it under him, and he sat on it.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the list of places where one says a ברכה. It brings a פסוק showing where the stone משה sat on comes from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With the עוג story finished, the גמרא moves to the next item on the list. During the war with עמלק, משה's arms grew tired, so they placed a stone under him to sit on. Seeing that stone reminds a person of the miracle of that war.

phrases.english: And the stone that Moshe sat on:
as it is written: 'And Moshe's hands were heavy,'
'and they took a stone and put it under him,'
'and he sat on it.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the עוג story and goes back to explaining the items on the list.
steps.raayaObject: The stone משה sat on, which is an item on the list of places that get a ברכה

steps.title: Source for אשתו של לוט
steps.stepSummary: The next item is אשתו של לוט, and the פסוק says she turned into a pillar of salt.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the wife of לוט, as it says: 'And his wife looked back from behind him, and she became a pillar of salt.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the פסוק behind the next item on the list, אשתו של לוט.
steps.deeperAnalysis: She turned into a pillar of salt, so there is a physical place that a person could see. That is why she appears on the list of places where one says a ברכה.

phrases.english: And the wife of Lot:
as it says: 'And his wife looked back from behind him,'
'and she became a pillar of salt.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next item on the list, explained the same way.
steps.raayaObject: אשתו של לוט, an item on the list of places that get a ברכה

steps.title: Source for the wall of יריחו that was swallowed
steps.stepSummary: The next item is חומת יריחו, which sank down into the ground, and the גמרא gives the פסוק for it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the wall of יריחו that was swallowed, as it is written: 'And the wall fell down in its place.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the source for the last item here, the wall of יריחו that sank into the ground.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא calls the wall 'swallowed' and cites the פסוק 'ותפל החומה תחתיה' as its source. Here the item is only being listed. In step 22 the גמרא will ask how 'swallowed' fits a פסוק that says the wall 'fell', and step 23 answers.

keyTerms.meaning: that was swallowed (sank into the ground)

phrases.english: And the wall of Jericho that was swallowed:
as it is written: 'And the wall fell down in its place.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next item on the list, explained the same way.
steps.raayaObject: חומת יריחו that sank into the ground, an item on the list of places that get a ברכה

steps.title: Why bless over אשתו של לוט if her story was a punishment
steps.stepSummary: All the other items on the list are miracles, but אשתו של לוט turning to salt was a punishment. So why say a ברכה on seeing her?
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense for all the others, because they are miracles. But אשתו של לוט was a punishment!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the list. Every other item is a happy miracle, but אשתו של לוט was a disaster, so why would someone bless when seeing her?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא grouped אשתו של לוט with miracles like the stone משה sat on and the wall of יריחו. A blessing of thanks fits a miracle that saved people. It does not seem to fit a story where someone was punished and killed.

phrases.english: It makes sense for all of them, they are miracles,
phrases.notes: בשלמא means: I understand this part.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אִשְׁתּוֹ שֶׁל לוֹט פּוּרְעָנוּתָא הוּא!
phrases.english: but Lot's wife is a punishment!
phrases.notes: This is the part that does not fit.

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא כּוּלְּהוּ נִיסָּא, אֶלָּא אִשְׁתּוֹ שֶׁל לוֹט פּוּרְעָנוּתָא הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the list item from step 15 and questions why it is there.
steps.kashyaTarget: Including אשתו של לוט in a list of places where you say a blessing for a miracle
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A miracle blessing praises ה׳ for saving people. אשתו של לוט was punished, not saved.

steps.title: Over אשתו של לוט one says ״דיין האמת״
steps.stepSummary: The blessing over אשתו של לוט is not a thank-you blessing. It is ״ברוך דיין האמת״, the blessing said over bad news.
steps.simpleTranslation: He says: 'Blessed… the true Judge.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that seeing אשתו של לוט does get a ברכה, but a different one: ״דיין האמת״, which accepts ה׳'s judgment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question assumed every item gets the same happy blessing. The answer is that the type of blessing matches the event. A punishment gets the blessing for hard news.

keyTerms.meaning: The true Judge, the blessing said over bad news

phrases.english: He says: 'Blessed… the true Judge.'
phrases.notes: The '…' stands for the usual opening words of a blessing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 17.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every place on the list gets a happy thank-you blessing.
steps.terutzMaskana: אשתו של לוט gets ״דיין האמת״, the blessing for bad news.

steps.title: But the ברייתא says the blessing is thanks and praise
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא says all these items get 'thanks and praise.' ״דיין האמת״ is not thanks and praise, so the answer does not fit.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it teaches 'thanks and praise'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer. The ברייתא said all these sights get thanks and praise, and ״דיין האמת״ is not that.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The previous answer fixed the logic but broke the wording. The ברייתא gives one heading for the whole list, thanks and praise. A blessing over bad news does not fit under that heading.

phrases.english: But it teaches 'thanks and praise'!
phrases.notes: והא is how a challenge from a source starts: 'but look, it says...'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 18.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that אשתו של לוט gets ״דיין האמת״
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא calls every blessing on the list 'thanks and praise'. ״דיין האמת״ is not praise for a good thing.

steps.title: Two blessings: one for אשתו של לוט and one for לוט
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא is reworded: for לוט and his wife there are two blessings. ״דיין האמת״ is for his wife, and ״זוכר את הצדיקים״ is for לוט.
steps.simpleTranslation: Teach it this way: over לוט and his wife one says two blessings. Over his wife he says 'Blessed… the true Judge,' and over לוט he says 'Blessed… Who remembers the righteous.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the wording of the ברייתא. The place gets two blessings: a sad one for אשתו של לוט and a thankful one for לוט, who was saved.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the 'thanks and praise' heading works, because לוט's rescue is a real miracle that gets a thankful blessing. The ״דיין האמת״ blessing for his wife is added on top. Both the logic and the wording now fit.
steps.confusionAlert: תני here does not mean a new ברייתא is being quoted. It means the גמרא is changing the wording of the one it already has.

phrases.english: Teach it this way: over Lot and over his wife
phrases.notes: The ברייתא's wording is being fixed.

phrases.english: one says two blessings.
Over his wife he says: 'Blessed… the true Judge,'

phrases.aramaic: וְעַל לוֹט אוֹמֵר ״בָּרוּךְ … זוֹכֵר אֶת הַצַּדִּיקִים״.
phrases.english: and over Lot he says: 'Blessed… Who remembers the righteous.'
phrases.notes: This is the thankful blessing that fits 'thanks and praise'.

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנִי: עַל לוֹט וְעַל אִשְׁתּוֹ מְבָרְכִים שְׁתַּיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 19 by rewording the ברייתא.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The place of אשתו של לוט gets only one blessing, so the 'thanks and praise' heading does not fit it.
steps.terutzMaskana: There are two blessings, and לוט's rescue gives the 'thanks and praise' part.
steps.whatToRemember: At the place of אשתו של לוט you say two blessings: ״דיין האמת״ for her punishment and ״זוכר את הצדיקים״ for לוט's rescue.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: ה׳ remembers the righteous even when He is angry
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן shows from a פסוק that even while ה׳ destroyed סדום, He remembered אברהם and saved לוט. This is the basis for the blessing ״זוכר את הצדיקים״.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: Even at a time of the anger of הקדוש ברוך הוא, He remembers the righteous, as it says: 'And it was, when God destroyed the cities of the plain, God remembered אברהם and sent לוט out of the destruction, etc.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings רבי יוחנן to show where the idea behind ״זוכר את הצדיקים״ comes from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says that in the middle of destroying סדום, ה׳ 'remembered אברהם' and pulled לוט out. לוט was saved because of אברהם. This is exactly the wording of the blessing over לוט.

keyTerms.meaning: At the time of His anger
The cities of the plain (סדום and its neighbors)

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ בִּשְׁעַת כַּעֲסוֹ שֶׁל הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא,
phrases.english: Even at a time of the anger of the Holy One, Blessed be He,
He remembers the righteous,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וַיְהִי בְּשַׁחֵת אֱלֹהִים אֶת עָרֵי הַכִּכָּר
phrases.english: as it says: 'And it was, when God destroyed the cities of the plain,'
'God remembered Abraham'

phrases.aramaic: וַיְשַׁלַּח אֶת לוֹט מִתּוֹךְ הַהֲפֵכָה וְגוֹ׳״.
phrases.english: 'and sent Lot out of the destruction, etc.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: אֲפִילּוּ בִּשְׁעַת כַּעֲסוֹ שֶׁל הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the blessing ״זוכר את הצדיקים״ from step 20.
steps.raayaObject: The blessing ״זוכר את הצדיקים״ said over לוט
steps.raayaSupportSource: בראשית יט:כט, 'ויזכר אלהים את אברהם וישלח את לוט'

steps.title: Did the wall of יריחו sink, or did it fall
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא says the wall of יריחו was swallowed into the ground, but the פסוק says it fell.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And the wall of יריחו that was swallowed.' Was the wall of יריחו swallowed? But it fell, as it says: 'And it was, when the people heard the sound of the שופר, the people shouted a great shout, and the wall fell in its place'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next item in the ברייתא again, the wall of יריחו, so it can question it. The פסוק seems to say the wall fell, not that it sank.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 16 only listed this item. Here the גמרא repeats the words in order to attack them. 'Swallowed' means sinking into the ground, while 'fell' means toppling over, so the two descriptions seem to clash.

keyTerms.meaning: Was swallowed, sank into the ground
In its place, flat where it stood

phrases.english: 'And the wall of Jericho that was swallowed.'
phrases.notes: The words of the ברייתא are quoted again.

phrases.english: Was the wall of Jericho swallowed?
But it fell, as it says:
'And it was, when the people heard the sound of the shofar,'
'the people shouted a great shout,'
'and the wall fell in its place'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the list item from step 16 and questions it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's description of the wall of יריחו as 'swallowed'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק says the wall 'fell', which seems different from sinking into the ground.

steps.title: The wall was as wide as it was tall, so it had to sink
steps.stepSummary: The wall's width equaled its height, so simply falling over would not open the city. It sank into the ground.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since its width and its height were equal to each other, that is why it was completely swallowed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that because the wall was as thick as it was high, toppling over would not help. So it sank straight down, and the פסוק's 'fell in its place' means it went down where it stood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A square-shaped wall that tips over is still a wall of the same size, so the city would stay blocked. The only way it could stop blocking was to go down into the ground. So 'fell' and 'swallowed' describe the same event.

phrases.english: Since its width and its height
were equal to each other,
that is why it was completely swallowed.
phrases.notes: Falling over would not have opened the city.

steps.triggerLanguage: כֵּיוָן דְּפוּתְיַהּ וְרוּמַהּ כִּי הֲדָדֵי נִינְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 22.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Bringing the פסוק and the ברייתא together
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Fell' means it toppled over, which does not match 'swallowed'.
steps.terutzMaskana: Toppling would not have helped, so the wall went down where it stood, into the ground.

steps.title: Four kinds of people must give thanks
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה in the name of רב says four people must thank ה׳: sea travelers, desert travelers, a sick person who recovered, and a prisoner who was freed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: Four must give thanks: those who go down to the sea, those who travel through deserts, one who was sick and was healed, and one who was locked in prison and came out.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins. רב lists four people who were in danger and were saved, and who must thank ה׳.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now the topic was blessings on seeing places of miracles. Now the topic shifts to people who were personally saved. Each of the four went through real danger and came out safe.

keyTerms.meaning: Those who go down to the sea, sea travelers

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for ברכת הגומל, which is still said today by people who were saved from these dangers.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said in the name of Rav:
Four must give thanks:
those who go down to the sea, those who travel through deserts,
and one who was sick and was healed,

phrases.aramaic: וּמִי שֶׁהָיָה חָבוּשׁ בְּבֵית הָאֲסוּרִים וְיָצָא.
phrases.english: and one who was locked in prison and came out.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב: אַרְבָּעָה צְרִיכִין לְהוֹדוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: thanking ה׳ for being personally saved.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sea travelers, desert travelers, a sick person who recovered, and a freed prisoner must all thank ה׳.

steps.title: Source for sea travelers thanking ה׳
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source that יורדי הים must thank ה׳. It answers with a chain of פסוקים from תהלים קז: danger at sea, crying out, calm, and thanks.
steps.simpleTranslation: How do we know that sea travelers must thank ה׳? Because it says: 'Those who go down to the sea in ships... they saw the works of ה׳.' And it says: 'He raised a stormy wind... they go up to the sky, they go down to the depths.' And it says: 'They reel and stagger like a drunk.' And it says: 'They cried to ה׳ in their trouble, and He took them out of their distress.' And it says: 'He turns the storm into calm.' And it says: 'They were happy because the waters became quiet.' And it says: 'Let them thank ה׳ for His kindness and His wonders for people.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins proving each part of רב's list. It starts with sea travelers and quotes the section of תהלים about a storm at sea.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The many ״ואומר״ lines each add one stage of the story: the danger, the panic, the prayer, the rescue, and the calm. The last stage, ״יודו לה׳ חסדו״, is the actual source for the obligation to thank. The earlier פסוקים show who that line is speaking about.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know this? (a request for a source)
Those who go down to the sea; sea travelers
And it (the פסוק) also says; adds another verse
Let them thank ה׳ for His kindness; the key phrase for the obligation

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think each ״ואומר״ is a separate proof. Together they form one story. The thanking at the end applies to the people who went through the danger described before it.

phrases.english: Sea travelers, from where do we know (that they must thank)?
As it is written: 'Those who go down to the sea in ships, etc.'
'they saw the works of ה׳.'
And it says: 'He raised a stormy wind'
'they go up to the sky, they go down to the depths,'
and it says: 'They reel and stagger like a drunk,'
and it says: 'They cried to ה׳ in their trouble'
'and He took them out of their distress,'
and it says: 'He turns the storm into calm,'
and it says: 'They were happy because (the waters) became quiet,'
and it says: 'Let them thank ה׳ for His kindness'
phrases.notes: The source for the obligation to give thanks.

phrases.english: 'and His wonders for people.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the scriptural source for the first item in רב's list from step 24.
steps.raayaObject: רב's rule that יורדי הים must thank ה׳
steps.raayaSupportSource: תהלים קז:כג–לא: storm at sea, prayer, calm, and ״יודו לה׳ חסדו״

steps.title: Source for desert travelers thanking ה׳
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source that הולכי מדברות must thank ה׳. It answers from the section of תהלים קז about people lost in the desert who cried out, were led on a straight path, and gave thanks.
steps.simpleTranslation: How do we know that desert travelers must thank ה׳? Because it says: 'They wandered in the desert, in a wasteland, on a road; they did not find a city to live in... They cried to ה׳... He led them on a straight path... Let them thank ה׳ for His kindness.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the second item on רב's list, desert travelers. It quotes the earlier section of the same chapter in תהלים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The pattern is the same as for the sea. The danger is being lost with no city to find. They pray, ה׳ guides them on a straight road, and then comes ״יודו לה׳ חסדו״. The ״…″ marks show the גמרא is skipping parts of the פסוקים and quoting only the key stages.

phrases.english: Desert travelers, from where do we know (that they must thank)?
As it is written: 'They wandered in the desert, in a wasteland, on a road'
'they did not find a city to live in...'
'They cried to ה׳...'
'He led them on a straight path...'
'Let them thank ה׳ for His kindness.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Same method as step 25, applied to the second item in רב's list.
steps.raayaObject: רב's rule that הולכי מדברות must thank ה׳
steps.raayaSupportSource: תהלים קז:ד–ח: lost in the desert, prayer, guidance, and ״יודו לה׳ חסדו״

steps.title: Source for a sick person who recovered thanking ה׳
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings the source that מי שחלה ונתרפא must thank ה׳. It uses the section of תהלים קז about people who became sick, could not eat, cried out, were healed, and gave thanks.
steps.simpleTranslation: A person who was sick and got better must thank ה׳, as it is written: 'Foolish people, because of their sinful ways and their wrongdoings, suffer. Their soul hates all food... They cried to ה׳ in their trouble... He sent His word and healed them... Let them thank ה׳ for His kindness.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the source for the third item on the list, someone who was sick and recovered. Here it does not even ask ״מנלן״; it goes straight to the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this case the danger is illness: the sick person is so weak that he hates all food. Then comes the prayer, then ה׳ heals them, and then ״יודו לה׳ חסדו״. So the same four-stage pattern teaches the obligation to thank.

keyTerms.meaning: One who was sick and recovered

phrases.english: One who was sick and recovered (must thank), as it is written:
'Fools, because of their sinful ways'
'and because of their wrongdoings, suffer.'
'Their soul hates all food, etc.'

phrases.aramaic: וַיִּזְעֲקוּ אֶל ה׳ בַּצַּר לָהֶם וְגוֹ׳
phrases.english: 'They cried to ה׳ in their trouble, etc.'
'He sent His word and healed them, etc.'
'Let them thank ה׳ for His kindness.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Same method as steps 25–26, applied to the third item in רב's list.
steps.raayaObject: רב's rule that a sick person who recovered must thank ה׳
steps.raayaSupportSource: תהלים קז:יז–כא: illness, prayer, healing, and ״יודו לה׳ חסדו״

steps.title: Source for a freed prisoner thanking ה׳
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source that a prisoner who was freed must thank ה׳. It answers with the section of תהלים קז about people sitting in darkness who were humbled, cried out, were taken out, and gave thanks.
steps.simpleTranslation: How do we know that someone who was locked in prison must thank ה׳? Because it says: 'Those who sit in darkness and the shadow of death... because they rebelled against the words of God...' And it says: 'He humbled their heart with hard labor...' And it says: 'They cried to ה׳ in their trouble.' And it says: 'He took them out of darkness and the shadow of death...' And it says: 'Let them thank ה׳ for His kindness.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source for the fourth and last item on רב's list, a freed prisoner. This finishes the proofs for all four people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the danger is being locked in a dark prison, described as ״חושך וצלמות״. Again the stages are trouble, prayer, release from the darkness, and then ״יודו לה׳ חסדו״. All four cases come from the same chapter and follow the same pattern.
steps.whatToRemember: All four people in רב's list (sea travelers, desert travelers, a sick person who recovered, and a freed prisoner) come from תהלים קז. Each section has the same pattern: danger, then crying out to ה׳, then rescue, then ״יודו לה׳ חסדו״. That last phrase is the source for the obligation to thank ה׳, which we fulfill today with ברכת הגומל.
steps.whyThisMatters: This list of four is the basis for who says ברכת הגומל in practice.

phrases.aramaic: מִי שֶׁהָיָה חָבוּשׁ בְּבֵית הָאֲסוּרִין מְנָלַן? —
phrases.english: One who was locked in prison, from where do we know (that he must thank)?
As it is written: 'Those who sit in darkness and the shadow of death, etc.'
'because they rebelled against the words of God, etc.'
And it says: 'He humbled their heart with hard labor, etc.'
and it says: 'They cried to ה׳ in their trouble,'
and it says: 'He took them out of darkness and the shadow of death, etc.'
and it says: 'Let them thank ה׳ for His kindness.'

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי שֶׁהָיָה חָבוּשׁ בְּבֵית הָאֲסוּרִין מְנָלַן? — דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the series of sources for רב's list of four from step 24.
steps.raayaObject: רב's rule that a freed prisoner must thank ה׳
steps.raayaSupportSource: תהלים קז:י–טו: imprisonment in darkness, humbling, prayer, release, and ״יודו לה׳ חסדו״

steps.title: What blessing does he say?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what words the four people say when they thank ה׳.
steps.simpleTranslation: What blessing does he say?
steps.whatsHappening: We know these four people must thank ה׳, and now the גמרא asks for the actual words. This short question sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier steps proved that thanks is required. They did not say what the thanks sounds like. This question moves from 'who must thank' to 'how to thank'.

phrases.english: What blessing does he say?
phrases.notes: Refers to any of the four people from Step 24.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows the proofs from תהלים קז and asks for the actual wording of the thanks.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The text of the blessing of thanks.

steps.title: The wording of the blessing
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה says the blessing is ״ברוך גומל חסדים טובים״.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: "Blessed is the One Who does good kindnesses."
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה gives the words of the blessing. It praises ה׳ for doing kindness.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The blessing fits all four cases, because each person was saved from danger through ה׳'s kindness. This is the source of what we call ברכת הגומל.

keyTerms.meaning: the name of this blessing of thanks

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the basis of the ברכת הגומל people say today after a trip or recovering from illness.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said:
"Blessed is the One Who does good kindnesses."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 29.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The blessing is ״ברוך גומל חסדים טובים״.

steps.title: The thanks must be said before ten people
steps.stepSummary: אביי adds that the thanks must be said in front of ten people, learned from ״בקהל עם״.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: And he must give thanks in front of ten people, as it is written: "Let them exalt Him in the congregation of the people."
steps.whatsHappening: אביי adds a new rule: this blessing is not said alone, but in front of ten people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof is the next פסוק in the same chapter (תהלים קז:לב). The word קהל, 'congregation', means a group, and a group in this sense means at least ten.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
And he must give thanks in front of ten,
as it is written:
"Let them exalt Him in the congregation of the people, etc."
phrases.notes: תהלים קז:לב. A קהל is understood as at least ten.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַבָּיֵי אָמַר: וְצָרִיךְ לְאוֹדוֹיֵי קַמֵּי עַשְׂרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a requirement about how the blessing from Step 30 is said.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The thanksgiving blessing must be said before ten people.

steps.title: Two of the ten must be Torah scholars
steps.stepSummary: מר זוטרא adds that two of the ten must be רבנן, learned from ״ובמושב זקנים״.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר זוטרא said: And two of them must be רבנן, as it says: "And praise Him in the seat of the elders."
steps.whatsHappening: מר זוטרא adds another detail: among the ten, two must be Torah scholars.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The second half of the same פסוק mentions זקנים, 'elders', which means scholars. Since the word is plural, the minimum is two.

phrases.english: Mar Zutra said:
And two of them must be Sages,
as it is said:
"And in the seat of the elders praise Him."
phrases.notes: Since 'elders' is plural, it means at least two.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָר זוּטְרָא אָמַר: וּתְרֵין מִינַּיְיהוּ רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on אביי's ten by reading the second half of the same פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two of the ten must be Torah scholars.

steps.title: Maybe all ten must be scholars
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי challenges: why only two scholars? Maybe all of them must be רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי objected: Why not say that all of them must be רבנן?!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי attacks מר זוטרא's reading. If the פסוק talks about elders, maybe the whole group has to be scholars.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מר זוטרא split the פסוק: ten from ״קהל עם״ and two scholars from ״זקנים״. רב אשי asks why we don't read both halves as describing one group of all scholars.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi objected to it:
But say that all of them must be Sages?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges מר זוטרא's reading in Step 32.
steps.kashyaTarget: מר זוטרא's rule that only two of the ten must be scholars.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק mentions elders; nothing forces us to limit it to two rather than the whole group.

steps.title: The verse says 'people,' not 'elders'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers: the פסוק says ״בקהל עם״, a congregation of regular people, not a congregation of elders.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is it written "in the congregation of elders"? "In the congregation of the people" is written!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends מר זוטרא: the main group is described as 'people', so not everyone has to be a scholar.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the ten are called ״עם״, the group is made of ordinary people. The scholars are only a part of them, so the requirement is just two.

phrases.english: Is it written "in the congregation of elders"?
"In the congregation of the people" is written.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב אשי's objection in Step 33.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Precise reading of the פסוק's wording
steps.terutzHavaAmina: All of the group must be scholars.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ten are ordinary people (עם), and only two among them need to be scholars.

steps.title: Maybe ten regular people plus two scholars
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: maybe we need ten ordinary people and two extra scholars, twelve total. This question is left unanswered: קשיא.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say: ten from the rest of the people, and two רבנן in addition! This is a קשיא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new challenge: maybe the two scholars are on top of the ten, not part of them. No answer is found, so it ends with 'קשיא'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק has two groups: 'people' and 'elders'. It could mean two separate groups, adding up to twelve. The גמרא cannot disprove this, so the question stays open, but the halacha is not thrown out.
steps.confusionAlert: קשיא at the end does not mean the rule of ten with two scholars is canceled. It only means this particular question was not answered.

phrases.english: But say ten from the rest of the people,
and two Sages in addition!
It is difficult.
phrases.notes: The question stands without an answer.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After Step 34 rejected 'all scholars', this offers another reading that is not rejected.
steps.kashyaTarget: מר זוטרא's claim that the two scholars are counted within the ten.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק names two groups, so the scholars could be in addition to the ten ordinary people.

steps.title: רב יהודה recovers and his visitors bless for him
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה got sick and recovered. רב חנא בגדתאה and other רבנן visited and blessed ה׳ for him, and he said that this exempted him from thanking.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה was sick and recovered. רב חנא בגדתאה and the רבנן came to visit him. They said to him: "Blessed is the Merciful One Who gave you to us and did not give you to the dust." He said to them: "You have exempted me from giving thanks."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story. The visitors' blessing counted as רב יהודה's ברכת הגומל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This shows that someone else can say the blessing of thanks for the person who was saved. It also shows the words do not have to be exactly ״גומל חסדים טובים״, since a blessing of thanks in other words worked.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda was sick and recovered.

phrases.aramaic: עָל לְגַבֵּיהּ רַב חָנָא בַּגְדָּתָאָה וְרַבָּנַן.
phrases.english: Rav Chana of Baghdad and the Sages came in to visit him.
They said to him:
"Blessed is the Merciful One Who gave you to us
and did not give you to the dust."
He said to them:
You have exempted me from giving thanks.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the derivation of the requirements to a story showing how the blessing was fulfilled in practice.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A blessing of thanks said by others in the presence of the recovered person can exempt him.

steps.title: Doesn't אביי require ten people?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the story: אביי said the thanks must be said before ten, so how did this visit count?
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't אביי say one must give thanks in front of ten?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how the story fits with אביי's rule from Step 31.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story only mentions רב חנא and some רבנן visiting. If there were fewer than ten, the blessing should not have counted.

phrases.english: But didn't Abaye say
one must give thanks in front of ten!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the story in Step 36 using אביי's rule.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יהודה's claim that he was exempted.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Thanks requires ten people, and the story does not show ten were there.

steps.title: Ten people were there
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that there were ten people present.
steps.simpleTranslation: There were ten there.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers simply: the visitors numbered ten, so אביי's rule was kept.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story did not mention the count, but the group was large enough. So there is no conflict with אביי.

phrases.english: There were ten there.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 37.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Clarifying the facts of the case
steps.terutzMaskana: Ten were present, so אביי's requirement was met.

steps.title: But he himself did not give thanks
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: רב יהודה himself never said the blessing, so how was he exempt?
steps.simpleTranslation: But he himself did not give thanks!
steps.whatsHappening: A second challenge: the obligation is on the person who recovered, but here only the visitors spoke.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule says the sick person who recovered must thank. רב יהודה stayed silent, so how was his own obligation done?

phrases.english: But he himself did not give thanks!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the ten-person issue is solved, a new problem with the story is raised.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The obligation belongs to the person who recovered, and he did not say the blessing.

steps.title: Answering אמן counts as blessing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that he did not need to say it himself, because he answered אמן after their blessing.
steps.simpleTranslation: He did not need to, because he answered "אמן" after them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that answering אמן to someone else's blessing is like saying the blessing yourself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By saying אמן, רב יהודה joined himself to the visitors' blessing. That counts as if he said it, so his obligation was fulfilled.
steps.whatToRemember: ברכת הגומל is ״ברוך גומל חסדים טובים״, said before ten, two of them scholars. Someone else can say it for the person who was saved, if ten are present and he answers אמן.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is an important general rule: answering אמן after a blessing counts like saying the blessing yourself.

phrases.english: He did not need to,
because he answered "Amen" after them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 39 and closes the story.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Introducing a general principle (answering אמן counts as reciting)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only the person who recovered saying the words himself fulfills the obligation.
steps.terutzMaskana: Answering אמן after others' blessing counts as his own thanks.

steps.title: Three people who need protection
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה lists three kinds of people who need to be watched over: a sick person, a חתן, and a כלה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: Three kinds of people need protection. They are a sick person, a groom, and a bride.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new statement of רב יהודה that groups three types of people together. They all need extra guarding from harm.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just before this, the גמרא discussed the list of four people who must thank ה׳, which רב יהודה taught in the name of רב. So it now brings another teaching of רב יהודה that groups several cases into one category. רש״י explains that they need guarding from מזיקין.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said:
Three require protection,
and these are they: a sick person, a groom, and a bride.
phrases.notes: רש״י explains that they need protection from harmful forces (מזיקין).

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה: שְׁלֹשָׁה צְרִיכִין שִׁימּוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new, related teaching of רב יהודה. It is brought because the earlier discussion also involved one of his lists of categories.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A sick person, a חתן, and a כלה need to be guarded.

steps.title: A ברייתא adds more people to the list
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא lists four: a sick person, a woman after childbirth, a חתן, and a כלה. Other opinions add a mourner, and תלמידי חכמים at night.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא teaches: a sick person, a woman who just gave birth, a groom, and a bride need protection. Some say a mourner too. And some say Torah scholars at night too.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with a longer version of רב יהודה's list. It also brings two more opinions that add even more people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא adds the חיה, a woman who has just given birth. The יש אומרים add an אבל, a mourner, and then תלמידי חכמים at night. רש״י explains that they need guarding from מזיקין: a sick person, a חיה and an אבל because their מזל is weakened, and a חתן, a כלה and תלמידי חכמים because the מזיקין are jealous of them.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in a ברייתא (a teaching from the time of the משנה that is not in the משנה itself)
A woman who has just given birth

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read 'חיה' here as 'animal.' In this context it means a woman who just gave birth.

phrases.english: It was taught in a baraita:
a sick person, a woman after childbirth, a groom, and a bride.
And some say: even a mourner.

phrases.aramaic: וְיֵשׁ אוֹמְרִים: אַף תַּלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים בַּלַּיְלָה.
phrases.english: And some say: even Torah scholars at night.
phrases.notes: רש״י: the מזיקין attack them out of jealousy.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Expands רב יהודה's list with a parallel ברייתא and additional opinions.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A sick person, a חיה, a חתן, and a כלה need protection. According to some, so does an אבל, and so do תלמידי חכמים at night.

steps.title: Three things that lengthen life
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה says that taking a long time in three things lengthens a person's life: תפלה, the meal at his table, and the bathroom.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב יהודה said: There are three things that, if a person takes a long time with them, his days and years are lengthened. They are: one who takes long in his prayer, one who takes long at his table, and one who takes long in the bathroom.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another 'list of three' from רב יהודה. These are three activities where taking your time brings a longer life.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a new teaching connected only by being another group of three from the same אמורא. The list mixes a spiritual act (תפלה), a social and religious act (the meal at one's table), and a bodily act (the bathroom). The גמרא will soon question and explain the items.

keyTerms.meaning: One who lengthens, or takes a long time
They lengthen his days and years (long life)

phrases.english: And Rav Yehuda said:
Three matters, the one who prolongs them
they lengthen a person's days and years.
One who prolongs his prayer,
and one who prolongs his time at his table,
and one who prolongs his time in the bathroom.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה: שְׁלֹשָׁה דְּבָרִים הַמַּאֲרִיךְ בָּהֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another statement of רב יהודה, brought next because it is also a list of three.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Taking one's time in תפלה, at the meal, and in the bathroom lengthens life.

steps.title: Is a long prayer really a good thing?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the first item: is taking a long time in תפלה really a virtue? It begins quoting רבי חייא בר אבא in the name of רבי יוחנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: And one who prolongs his prayer, is that a good thing? But didn't רבי חייא בר אבא say in the name of רבי יוחנן:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions רב יהודה's first item. It starts bringing a source that seems to say a long תפלה is not good. The quote itself continues on the next amud, so this step is setting up the challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יהודה praised a long תפלה. The גמרא now points to רבי יוחנן, who will say that someone who prays long and expects his prayer to be answered ends up with heartache. That looks like a direct contradiction, and the answer will come next.

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't [so-and-so] say? (introduces a contradicting source)

steps.confusionAlert: The sentence is cut off at the end of the amud. The actual words of רבי יוחנן come at the start of the next amud.

phrases.english: And one who prolongs his prayer, is that a virtue?
But didn't Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba say
that Rabbi Yoḥanan said:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the first item of רב יהודה's list in Step 43.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יהודה's claim that a long תפלה lengthens life.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוחנן's statement, quoted next, seems to say a long תפלה leads to heartache. That clashes with calling it a virtue.
